title: Data sovereignty and logging intake - Marigold Bank
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-08-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
End: 15:57 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording link: (redacted)

Optional auto sections:
Summary: Intake call to surface Marigold Bank's data residency and logging constraints across hosted/dedicated/private options. Customer wants EU-only processing for account linking, strict audit logs, retention limits and proof of no model retraining on customer data. Redwood AE/SE covered architecture options and potential POC path.
Topics: GDPR residency, HIPAA question for health-adjacent payments, SOC2 + ISO ask, log redaction and retention, BYOK/HSM, dedicated cluster sizing, legal/subprocessors.
Action items (in transcript body and top): see action_items field.
Transcription quality: medium (occasional mis-hearings: K.V. cache -> K.V. cash; H.P.A.A. -> HIPAA, etc.)

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Trujillo: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sofia, AE on the Redwood side. Marcus and Leah from our team are here. Thanks Marigold for the time.
[00:12] Alice Morgan: Hi Sofia, thanks. I'm Alice, Head of Security at Marigold. We scheduled this to figure out residency restraints and what logs you keep by default.
[00:18] Marcus Chen: Great. Quick agenda: understand the types of data you'll send to the API, residency/region constraints, retention and redaction needs, then map to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options.
[00:30] Tom Reeves: For context, we're a regulated banking app, pan-EU customers, some UK-only accounts. We cannot allow cardholder data or certain personal identifiers to leave EU systems.
[00:40] Benji Hale: Also want to confirm we won't have model owners retrain on our content — we need 'no training' contract language.
[00:48] Marcus Chen: Absolutely. Redwood's policy is no customer data used to train models by default for dedicated/private. For Hosted there are two modes — opt out for training — but we need contract language. We'll clarify.
[00:58] Priya Das: One immediate ask — do you provide a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and can that include EU-only subprocessors?
[01:05] Sofia Trujillo: Yes we have a DPA; we can provide it. For subprocessors, hosted mode uses cloud providers and a set of subprocessors that we list. For Private/on-prem we can avoid our cloud subprocessors.
[01:18] Alice Morgan: What about logs — request/response logs, audit logs, and model telemetry?
[01:23] Marcus Chen: By default in Hosted we retain request logs for 30 days for debugging and abuse detection, but we do offer a no-logs or reduced-logs option for enterprise customers — that's typically on Dedicated or Private.
[01:35] Alice Morgan: Reduced logs how? Like redacted PII?
[01:38] Marcus Chen: We can redact patterns server-side (SSNs, card numbers), we can also avoid storing response bodies entirely if you want. For Dedicated we can configure retention windows and push logs to your SIEM via VPC egress.
[01:50] Benji Hale: If we push logs to our SIEM, do you keep backups?
[01:54] Leah Ortiz: We can configure log forwarding with an agreement that no copies are retained in Redwood storage past the configured window. For private deployments you'd manage storage fully.
[02:05] Tom Reeves: Residency question: can we guarantee EU-only inference processing and no egress to the US for Hosted?
[02:12] Marcus Chen: On Hosted, we have EU regions (Frankfurt, Dublin) and UK region (London). For strict EU-only you probably want Dedicated in an EU-only tenancy or Private. Hosted has EU regional endpoints but note that control plane metadata and some telemetry can touch US systems unless contractualized.
[02:28] Alice Morgan: Can you enumerate that telemetry? We're particularly concerned about IP addresses, hashes of prompts, and audit sequences leaking to non-EU processors.
[02:38] Marcus Chen: Good question — telemetry can include anonymized usage metrics and service health, and some aggregated traces. We can provide an option to disable cross-region telemetry for Dedicated and entirely for Private.
[02:50] Priya Das: HIPAA — we do have a small vertical that takes healthcare-related payment instruments. Do you have a Business Associate Agreement (BAA)?
[02:59] Sofia Trujillo: Redwood can sign a BAA for Dedicated or Private deployments. Hosted support for HIPAA is limited and requires additional legal review. We'll flag that for follow-up.
[03:12] Benji Hale: Embeddings: we use embeddings for retrieval; do you persist embeddings and where?
[03:17] Marcus Chen: Embeddings are a separate storage concern. On Hosted embeddings are stored in region-backed object stores (and can be encrypted). On Dedicated we can dedicate the embeddings store in your VPC and on Private you host them. We can also support ephemeral embedding storage if you want no persistence.
[03:34] Alice Morgan: What's the difference then between Dedicated and Private in terms of control plane?
[03:40] Marcus Chen: Dedicated: customer gets reserved GPU pools and a VPC peering option; the control plane is still a managed Redwood service but we offer a private control plane tenancy feature for GDPR-heavy customers. Private: you get a customer-managed control plane in your environment or on-prem with full isolation.
[03:55] Alice Morgan: So for true EU residency + no-subprocessor guarantee, Private on-prem is the safest?
[03:59] Marcus Chen: Yes, or Dedicated with our private control plane + contractual subprocessor limitations.
[04:06] Tom Reeves: On encryption — BYOK? HSM? key rotation?
[04:10] Marcus Chen: We support Bring-Your-Own-Key via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM-backed keys for Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports customer-managed keys through cloud KMS in some tiers, but for HSM-backed keys you typically need Dedicated or Private.
[04:25] Priya Das: Auditability — we need immutable audit logs for compliance investigations for at least 7 years. Is that doable?
[04:33] Leah Ortiz: 7 years is long. For Dedicated we can export immutable logs into your archival store (S3 with Object Lock). For Hosted we retain shorter windows by default, but we can arrange archiving to your storage with the right contract and egress.
[04:48] Alice Morgan: What about access controls — RBAC, SSO, fine-grained roles?
[04:54] Marcus Chen: We integrate with SAML/SSO providers, SCIM for provisioning, and support row-level RBAC in the Console; Dedicated and Private give you stronger enforcement hooks.
[05:02] Benji Hale: Can we avoid Redwood support staff seeing request payloads?
[05:07] Marcus Chen: Yes — on Private and Dedicated with encrypted payloads and BYOK we can ensure support engineers don't have access. For Hosted we have redaction and role-based access controls, but in emergency we may access logs under strict process — we can add legal controls.
[05:20] Tom Reeves: Any part of Redwood models or telemetry used to tweak model weights with our customer data?
[05:26] Sofia Trujillo: No for Dedicated/Private. Hosted models are not trained on customer data by default, but we need contractual guarantee; we'll provide wording.
[05:34] Alice Morgan: Subprocessors: we need the full list and an attestation that none are US-based for EU-only promise.
[05:41] Marcus Chen: We'll share the current subprocessor list; that list changes with cloud provider choices. For Dedicated we can lock to EU-region providers. For Private there are no Redwood subprocessors for runtime.
[05:52] Priya Das: Let's talk specifc technical constraint: we have regulatory requirement to never store raw cardholder PAN. We tokenize card numbers before sending, but some flows still include last4 and BIN. Will Redwood logs contain last4 or any hash?
[06:05] Marcus Chen: By default we log request metadata; we can configure server-side redaction to strip last4 or hash it. We should put that in the workorder for the POC.
[06:15] Benji Hale: How about retention policy enforcement — do you have policy-as-code or policy configs?
[06:20] Marcus Chen: We have retention config per-route and per-customer on Dedicated; policies are enforced by orchestration layer. We'll show you the retention config UI in a demo.
[06:30] Alice Morgan: Tokenization question - embeddings storage linked to tokens, even if tokens are tokenized — can we avoid storing embeddings derived from any PAN derivatives?
[06:40] Marcus Chen: Yes, with data classification rules we'll not persist embeddings for endpoints that touch PAN-like tokens; we can mark routes as ephemeral.
[06:48] Tom Reeves: On logging granularity — we need to keep an immutable sequence of who invoked the route and which model variant served it, but not full request text for privacy. Possible?
[06:58] Leah Ortiz: Absolutely. We can keep signed audit entries pointing to a tombstone or redacted blob and we can also generate checksum/hashes with salt so you can verify integrity without revealing full content.
[07:10] Alice Morgan: Are the salts customer-controlled?
[07:12] Marcus Chen: On Dedicated/Private yes via BYOK or by configuring an HMAC secret.
[07:18] Priya Das: Can you provide an architecture diagram and sample config for a Dedicated EU-only deployment?
[07:23] Sofia Trujillo: Yes, Marcus will follow up with a proposed topology and the sizing.
[07:27] Marcus Chen: Quick note on performance trade-offs: if you avoid storing cache (prefix/KV cache) you may see 2-3x increase in token cost/latency depending on workload. We'll quantify during POC.
[07:41] Benji Hale: Good to know. For latency SLOs we need 95th percentile < 120ms for short prompts in EU region. Is that realistic for Dedicated?
[07:50] Marcus Chen: Yes for Dedicated GPU pools in EU we can tune for that SLO; we'll propose a sizing plan.
[07:58] Tom Reeves: Legal side: we'll need subprocessor appendices, DPA, BAA if HIPAA applies, and a security pack with SOC2/ISO docs.
[08:07] Sofia Trujillo: We will send the security pack and the DPA draft.
[08:10] Alice Morgan: Also need a clear statement about model weights never being fine-tuned on our data.
[08:14] Sofia Trujillo: We'll include explicit wording.
[08:16] [00:09:00] (participant joins late) Priya Das: Sorry late — quick question on eDiscovery for compliance investigations across EU customers if there's a lawful request.
[09:04] Marcus Chen: For Dedicated we can provide exports; for Hosted we follow legal process and can assist but must balance subprocessors.
[09:12] Alice Morgan: Are there any known customers in EU financial verticals using Dedicated?
[09:18] Sofia Trujillo: Yes — a couple of neo-banks and a payments processor. We'll share references under NDA.
[09:24] Benji Hale: On the subject of model fallback — if you run out of capacity in EU region does traffic ever route to US or other region?
[09:34] Marcus Chen: Default smart-routing prefers local region; fallback to other region is a configurable policy. For EU-only SLO you'd disable cross-region fallback.
[09:44] Tom Reeves: For the pilot we want to validate: 1) EU-only processing, 2) no retention of responses beyond X days, 3) no support visibility into raw payloads, 4) performance SLO.
[09:58] Sofia Trujillo: Good concise list. We'll scope a POC for those four items.
[10:04] Alice Morgan: Cost question: Dedicated vs Private — ballpark delta?
[10:08] Sofia Trujillo: Dedicated is typically a committed monthly capacity with clear unit economics; Private has higher upfront delivery and ops costs. We'll send a T-shirt sizing and cost ranges.
[10:16] Marcus Chen: For the POC we usually spin up a small dedicated cluster in EU with the private control-plane option so you can test both.
[10:26] Priya Das: Re: data subject rights (GDPR) — we need to be able to delete or export a user's data on request. Can Redwood support that?
[10:33] Marcus Chen: Yes — we have per-customer and per-route deletion APIs; on Dedicated/Private we can guarantee deletions from our stores and provide attestations. We'll show the deletion workflow.
[10:44] Alice Morgan: One more thing: PCI scope — we will never send raw PAN to the model, but if we ever do we'll need evidence you're outside of PCI scope. Do your customers claim PCI scope reduction?
[10:58] Leah Ortiz: Some customers reduce PCI scope by tokenizing and ensuring no PAN stored in provider logs. We'll help map controls but can't certify PCI on your behalf.
[11:09] Benji Hale: Can Redwood sign onto our standard security addendum?
[11:13] Sofia Trujillo: We'll review — many enterprise customers use their SAA with mutual edits.
[11:17] Tom Reeves: Great. On timeline — we are aiming for a pilot in Q4. Is that workable?
[11:22] Sofia Trujillo: Yes, Q4 pilot is doable. We will need SOC docs and DPA to proceed.
[11:27] (longer pause while slides referenced)
[11:38] Marcus Chen: I'll put together the EU Dedicated topology and retention config, plus an option for Private control plane.
[11:44] Priya Das: Can you also include a redaction matrix mapping PII/PHI types to redaction behavior?
[11:50] Marcus Chen: Yes.
[11:52] Alice Morgan: For audit evidence, we need signed logs for at least 2 years in immutable storage and availability to export on legal request. We can negotiate 7-year archiving via your export process.
[12:04] Leah Ortiz: We'll include the export path and options.
[12:08] Sofia Trujillo: Quick recap — Redwood to send: security pack (SOC2, ISO), DPA draft, BAA template, subprocessor list, EU Dedicated topology and sizing, retention and redaction config examples, and a POC proposal for Q4.
[12:24] Tom Reeves: Sounds good.
[12:26] Alice Morgan: We'll provide sample workloads and a contact in legal.
[12:30] Sofia Trujillo: Next steps we'll reflect in an email after this call. Thanks everyone.
[12:36] (call ends)
